why: Every seeded finding grades one document in isolation, so a gap in the shape of the set as a whole could not appear as one of them.

finding.title: No document shows a complete session from start to converged stop
finding.detail: SPEC.md defines the phases, protocol.md documents each command's payload, and SKILL.md carries a worked example written as instructions to an agent. None of them is a real session: there is no ledger a reader can open, no metrics.json to see the signals move, no report.md to see what the output actually looks like. A reader has to assemble the loop in their head from three documents before they can judge whether it is worth running.
finding.recommendation: Commit one real session to the repo and link it from the README, so the ledger, the metrics and the report can be read rather than described.

why: Zero dependencies is the most unusual property this tool has, and no pass had asked where a reader would find it stated.

finding.title: The zero-dependency guarantee is buried in a numbered non-negotiable
finding.detail: SPEC 8.5 says 'Zero npm dependencies. Node's standard library and psql only.' That is a headline property — it is why this can be symlinked into two harnesses and run anywhere node is — and it appears once, as item 5 of a list at the very bottom of a 377-line contract.
finding.recommendation: State it wherever a reader first meets the tool, not only where the contract enumerates its constraints.

why: The recommendation ended on a judgment about what the document becomes rather than a change somebody can make.

set.recommendation: Delete the 'No real-world session run yet' bullet, and replace it with a link to docs/example-session/ naming the subject, the pass count and the stop reason.

why: An unresolvable path is the first thing that breaks for an agent on another machine, which is the audience a skill is written for.
